Keywords: English charcoal carriers and forest tolls
RagShortTexts: The Forest Charter exempted back-carried wood and charcoal from the specified passage toll.

Variants.Content: Forest Charter clause14 limits chiminage to certain foresters and customary charges on outsiders’ commercial carts or packhorses carrying wood, bark and charcoal. People earning a living by carrying these on their backs are exempt from that toll. Fuel was both a household need and a laborer’s commodity; this exemption did not grant unrestricted cutting in anyone’s wood.

A charcoal carrier used personal labor to bring fuel to a buyer. The exemption removed a passage charge, not purchase costs or the need for cutting rights. Household fuel scarcity differed from the charges on commercial carts.
A forester had to distinguish authorized locations, commercial carts and back-carriers. Taxing every charcoal load ignored the exemption and expanded custody into arbitrary extraction.
